newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Slight rise in NZ terms of trade in Sep qtr.
newsitem.headline: Slight rise in NZ terms of trade in Sep qtr.

text.p: New Zealand's terms of trade rose by 0.2 percent in the September 1996 quarter, following a 0.7 percent fall in the June quarter, Statistics New Zealand said on Wednesday.
The index is now 0.2 percent higher than the September 1995 quarter, and 10.4 percent higher than the average level during the 1980s.
On a trade-weighted basis, the New Zealand dollar appreciated by 1.6 percent in the quarter and is now 6.4 percent higher than in the September 1995 quarter.

"The rise in the terms of trade means that returns from a fixed quantity of exports would have purchased 0.2 percent more in volume of imports in the September 1996 quarter than in the June 1996 quarter," SNZ said.

The September rise is the result of a 0.8 percent fall in export prices combined with a 0.9 percent fall in import prices. SNZ said prices of many key exports fell in the quarter, including aluminium (down 6.0 percent), dairy products (down 1.9 percent) and forestry products (down 2.0 percent).
